name: Nahua and Sahagún Florentine Codex natural-world account
description: Nahua elders, authors and artists collaborated with Bernardino de Sahagún on an illustrated bilingual manuscript whose Book 11 addresses the natural world.

impact.note: One manuscript recording knowledge its authors already held, long unpublished and changing little then; later scholarship on Nahua natural knowledge draws on it.

date.basis: Date of the cited witness; not a claim of origin.

events.statement: Getty dates completion of the collaborative Florentine Codex to 1577 and identifies Book 11 with natural things.

evidence.supports: Getty credits Nahua elders, authors and artists alongside Bernardino de Sahagún. It dates completion of the bilingual illustrated manuscript to 1577 and identifies Book 11 with natural things.
The Getty CONA catalogue gives circa 1578–1580 as its creation date, differing from the digital edition’s 1577 completion date.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped witness checked here; not the origin of the wider knowledge.

caveats: The manuscript is a colonial-era collaboration and does not date the origin of Nahua knowledge. Its completion date is a catalogued witness, not a claim that every component was composed in that year. Getty’s CONA catalogue dates creation to approximately 1578–1580, while its digital edition gives completion in 1577; these descriptions have not been reconciled.

research.note: Independent review checked the Getty digital edition’s completion statement and contributors, and found the separate Getty CONA catalogue date discrepancy.
